sections.h2: Whom do Woodford County, Kentucky owners call about a tax matter?
sections.html:
Questions about what a property is worth go to the Property Valuation Administrator. Questions about what you owe go to the sheriff. The valuation office is in the courthouse at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, Versailles, and the county directory shows it open from 8 each morning, closing at 4 Monday to Thursday and 5:30 on Friday. For the sheriff, the website gives 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126 and has bill search with online payment.

A notice stating each property's value reaches owners in spring. Bills leave the sheriff's office in the last week of September, and overdue notices follow in February. The sheriff warns that the office never mails threatening demands for property tax, so a letter from an unfamiliar "unit" with an 800 number should be reported, and the demand ignored.

sections.h2: What should a seller of a Woodford County house know?
sections.html:
Woodford covers 192 square miles of the Bluegrass and sits inside the Lexington metro area. Versailles holds the courthouse and the most people, while Midway is the lone second city. Neighbors are Fayette, Franklin, Scott, Jessamine, Mercer and Anderson. Lawmakers created the county in 1788 out of Fayette County, Virginia, naming it for General William Woodford, and it was the last of Kentucky's nine original counties. Scott and Franklin later took slices of it.

Labrot and Graham, the 1812 distillery behind Woodford Reserve, is here, along with Midway University, the Kentucky Castle and a youth outdoor program called the Life Adventure Center. A royal guest stayed at Lane's End Farm in 2007. Public schools include Woodford County High and Middle plus Huntertown, Northside, Southside and Simmons elementaries.

The 2020 through 2024 survey paints an affluent market:

  • The middle owned home is worth $299,700.
  • A typical household earns $83,788, and 9.7 percent of residents live in poverty.
  • Seven in ten households own (71.7 percent), and 40.7 percent of adults finished a bachelor's degree.
  • Rent runs $1,138. Owners pay $1,571 with a mortgage and $577 without.
  • There are 11,917 housing units, and builders pulled 95 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: How has the Woodford County population changed?
sections.html:
Growth here has been gradual. Headcounts of 14,434 in 1970, 23,208 in 2000, 24,939 in 2010 and 26,871 in 2020 lead to a 2025 estimate of 27,883, a 3.8 percent gain. In 2020 the median resident was 42.9 years old, and a fifth of the county (19.4 percent) had reached 65. There were 10,736 households in 11,487 housing units, with 6.5 percent of units empty, and 62.8 percent of people lived in urban areas. The latest survey lifts the 65 and over share to 22.5 percent and puts Hispanic or Latino residents at 9.4 percent.

Commuters average 24 minutes. The 2023 business census listed 618 employer establishments, 7,913 jobs and $340.1 million in payroll, and 2022 retail sales reached $321.5 million.

sections.h2: What is a Woodford County owner's tax year?
sections.html:
It follows the statewide calendar kept by the Department of Revenue and set out in KRS 134.015.

Yearly property tax steps for a Woodford County owner
WhenStep
January 1Values are set, and the owner of record on that day carries the tax
Opening Monday of May, 13 daysRoll on public display
25 to 35 days laterLocal appeals board sits
Up to November 1Pay 2 percent less
November 2 to December 31Pay the printed amount
JanuaryAdd 5 percent
February onwardAdd 10 percent
April 15Sheriff hands unpaid bills to the clerk, and a lien is recorded

Source: Kentucky Department of Revenue, The Property Tax Calendar, and KRS 134.015.

If you list in spring, last year's bill is still yours when your name was on the January 1 roll. Ask the sheriff for a written balance so the title company can pay it off.

sections.h2: How does a Woodford County owner challenge a value?
sections.html:
First, sit down with the PVA office. The state demands that conference, and the office has to walk you through how it reached your number and write down what each side claims. Then take the appeal to the County Clerk before business closes on the workday after the display period ends. With a May 3 to May 17 display, for example, the last day is May 18.

  • Bring proof: building and lot details, insurance papers, what the house cost to build, and listings of sales. An appeal without it is denied.
  • A professional you pay to speak for you must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or someone similarly recognized, and must carry your written permission.
  • Audio recording of the hearing is allowed, and the board must put any change in writing.

If you skip the local board, the Kentucky Claims Commission is closed to you. Where bills print before a case ends, and the final value tops your claim, you receive a supplemental bill for the gap.

sections.h2: Why are some Woodford County parcels valued differently?
sections.html:
The method depends on the property. Houses are compared to nearby sales, with adjustments for things like a basement. Barns and other farm structures are priced as replacement cost minus depreciation, and income property is valued from its earnings. Farmland is assessed on its agricultural worth under Section 172A of the state constitution, which can cut the tax on open pasture sharply. Anyone planning to divide a farm should ask both the PVA and the clerk what changes when the use changes.

Any parcel can be revalued yearly, and each must be inspected at least every fourth year. If your figure looks too high, ask the PVA which sales it relied on.

sections.h2: What does the Woodford County homestead exemption cover?
sections.html: Owners who reach 65, and the totally disabled, can have a fixed sum subtracted from the assessed value of the home they live in, one per household. File Form 62A350 at the PVA office. The exemption carries on while the same applicant stays. A veteran with a service connected disability rating, or anyone with a permanent Social Security disability finding, files once. A buyer applies fresh, and the PVA can quote the current sum, which the state revisits every two years.

sections.h2: What if a Woodford County bill is unpaid after April 15?
sections.html: Once the clerk records the lien, interest of 1 percent a month starts. A clerk commission of 10 percent comes next, and a 20 percent attorney commission after that. The attorney sends two notices, one at 30 days and one later, ahead of a sale 90 to 135 days after the transfer. Under KRS 134.420 the lien can last 11 years and travels with the parcel. At a sale it is paid out of your proceeds, and a private buyer who purchases the certificate may add fees.

faqs.q: Who sends out Woodford County tax bills each year?
faqs.a: The sheriff mails them during the last week of September. The sheriff's website lists 859-873-3119 and 859-873-3126 and provides bill search plus online payment.

faqs.q: How can a Woodford County owner push back on a valuation?
faqs.a: Schedule the PVA conference, then lodge the appeal with the County Clerk the next workday after public display ends. The PVA is at 103 S. Main Street, Room 108, in Versailles.

faqs.q: When does the 2 percent Woodford County discount stop?
faqs.a: It ends November 1. The printed amount is due until December 31, then 5 percent is added for January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: If a Woodford County house sells in spring, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is taxed and appears on the bill. The sale contract and title company decide who pays at closing, so get a written sheriff balance first.

faqs.q: What are good questions for the Woodford County PVA?
faqs.a: Ask which recent sales back your value and when staff last inspected the house. The answers tell you if an appeal is worth the effort before May.
